$note: Every top-level `<name>: t.router(` literal in apps/server/src/router.ts is accounted for exactly once, either as `migrated` (writes derived from a contract table) or in `pending` with the hand-written `.mutation(` keys it still carries. `total` may only go DOWN. A key in the router and not here is a finding; a key here and not in the router is a finding too — the census is not allowed to rot. A router in NEITHER list is a finding, so a whole new router cannot arrive unnoticed.

migrated.$note: Writes DERIVED from their contract tables — POD-380/381/382 (sessions), POD-1350 (layout), POD-731/732 (workflows), POD-729 (messages), POD-383 (superagent), POD-384 (machines/repos/discovery), POD-386 (specs), POD-2020 (interactions), POD-6418 (automations: its four writes on sync.submit, the routes thin LEGACY adapters), POD-6419 (superagent: its eight writes on sync.submit, every route a thin LEGACY adapter; shells: `forWorktree` on sync.submit, its start an effect record, the route a LEGACY adapter; hosts and the update panel's four commands on the plain command path), POD-6525 (messages: send, reply, inbox, dismiss, cancel, dismissNotice, spawnAgent and `sessions.ask` on sync.submit, the gate their adapter on tRPC and the relay with each transport's tag, the routes LEGACY adapters; `awaitAgent` stays a wait on its route, its claim retirement a write of its own). Zero hand-written mutations, with the single documented exception below. Adding one here is the regression these cutovers exist to prevent.

allowed.$note: `discovery.scan` scans CONVERSATIONS (`rpc.scan()` returns `{ conversations, diagnostics }`) and belongs to the session-discovery family; it shares the fleet router's name and nothing else, so POD-384 deliberately left it out of the fleet contract table. Allowlisted BY KEY and only on `discovery` — the same key under `repos` is still a finding. `layout` is POD-1350 — writes derived from LAYOUT_CONTRACTS via layoutFamilyProcedures(), zero hand-written mutations.

pending.$note: Routers whose writes are still hand-written, each with the issue that owns the migration. NOT this issue's scope; recorded so a new hand-written mutation cannot arrive unnoticed anywhere in router.ts. `keys: []` means the router serves reads only and must keep serving reads only.

settings.$note: THE GUARD. POD-313's title carves settings out of 3.3 explicitly (`settings via #352`), so this issue's obligation is that settings is UNTOUCHED — not that it shrinks. An added, removed or renamed key here is a finding in BOTH directions, and apps/server/src/router.settings-guard.test.ts checks the same claim against the RUNNING router.

cost.$note: Task cost reads (POD-1858). Reads only, and must keep serving reads only. Added by POD-6418, which found it in neither list.

operations.$note: Durable operations (POD-2097). `keys: []` is exact by this census's own definition — it counts hand-written `.mutation(` in router.ts, and this router's procedures are defined in apps/server/src/modules/operations/trpc.ts, the same shape as `updates`. It carries ONE write there, `operations.cancel`, and it is NOT yet derived from a contract table; the updater epic owns that migration. Recorded as pending rather than migrated so the claim stays true.

connect.$note: Podium Connect. `connect.check` is a QUERY: it asks the cloud to probe a public URL and returns the answer verbatim, storing nothing. Reads only, and must keep serving reads only.
